records.choice: New guide-voice narration built on the SOA-01 pattern: per-line TTS (speed 115, the lane's measured pace), speech-span trims on a gap timeline, the synthesized lane bed, mixed and mastered through the QC A-08 chain to ≈ −14 LUFS / TP ≤ −1, wrapped with the container intro/outro from WAV sources and encoded to AAC exactly once at render (A-09). A music-only twin programme (identical splice/timing) is kept for the voice-clone swap.

records.choice: Words pop into the planned empty lower band (centres y=1290/1410, alternating), centred at x=530, DejaVu Sans Bold 62px, chalk; key words amber with an overshoot pop. No plate, no band, no subtitle line anywhere in the DOM.

records.choice: Role: APPLY — the Academy ownership doctrine applied to one dated announcement (Alphabet Q3 2025: Gemini 650M monthly users). Payoff schedule (H4): the level lands first (L2), velocity re-earns attention (L3: 400M → 650M in five months), the turn states the mechanism plainly at L4 (walls / rules / memory — not theirs), L5 concedes the model's magnificence and names the room's owner, and L6 cashes the metaphor: 650 million guests, the house not theirs. The spoken ask (L7) and the bridge then spend the conviction the payoff earned. Objective (catalogue, GROUNDED): "Show 650 million monthly Gemini users meet the model inside Google's walls, keeping nothing for themselves."
records.alternatives: INTRODUCE (teach the ownership doctrine from zero) — rejected: that is the Toaster song's and Lesson 1's job; this lane reports a fact and applies the doctrine.
records.context: STRUCT-2's SOA-01 findings transferred: H5 weak (role unrecorded) and H4 weak (schedule unrecorded) — this record closes both for this piece at build time.
records.why: An unrecorded role drifts: the next SoA piece inherits the stance only if it is written down.
records.change: A lane-level ruling that SoA pieces teach rather than report.

records.element: End referral — bridge card after the spoken ask (H6 / HS-06)
records.choice: A bridge compartment after the spoken L7 ask (no narration over the card; the bed carries under it — CB-01), AFTER the ask's hold (content_end → +2.015s), IDENTICAL on every SOA piece (SOA-FIX lane standard): NEXT signpost → 'Renters can become owners.' → toaster symbol → 'WHO OWNS THE TOASTER?' → 'the song that asks who owns the layer' → 'tap to watch →'. Target: 'Who Owns the Toaster?', the funnel long-form. T-18: the title is never dropped bare — the same card says what it is (a song) and what it asks.
records.alternatives: (a) Dropping the script's spoken L7 ask because SOA-01 has none — rejected: the script is locked and its L7 does a different job (the N-09 channel ask, spoken, in the piece's own words) than the card (the HS-06 referral to the funnel piece). Both stay; the card comes after the ask's hold, so neither crowds the close. (b) Description/pinned-comment link only — rejected: it routes nobody from inside the piece (the STRUCT-2 H6 finding on SOA-01).
records.context: SOA-FIX (2026-10-24) made this card the lane standard after STRUCT-2 found H6 RANDOM-ABSENT on SOA-01. Funnel ruling: Toaster + Doorway are THE FUNNEL; shorts are judged by onward movement into them.
records.why: The objective ends at ownership; a viewer the close convinces is owed the route to the ownership teaching at the exact moment of conviction.
records.change: Funnel evidence (onward movement from this piece) at the 48-h scoreboard.

records.element: Visual grammar — the house fills, glows, and badges its guests
records.choice: Per the script's §7 note: a house cross-section fills floor by floor as the count climbs 400M → 650M (20 of 32 figures, then all 32), the walls re-draw amber at L4 (the landlord's house), and at L6 every figure turns amber — badged GUEST. The count is never a chart: it is a building people live in.
records.alternatives: A map or a growth curve — rejected: the piece's metaphor is tenancy; the visual must be a house.
records.context: The script's §7 visual template note is the design source; H7 (visual story performs the narration) is the governing class.
records.why: The visual grammar is the piece's argument made visible, chosen with the script — not decoration added at build.
records.change: Retention evidence against a beat at the 48-h scoreboard.
